RagShortTexts: The standing military of Kartli in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Kartli rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Kartli against overwhelming regional adversaries.

The spearmen form up on the road below the fortress, shields locked and spears set. The front rank takes the first charge of horsemen, and the rear files thrust through the gaps. A man who breaks the line will be dragged back by his comrades, and the captain's watchword is the only thing that keeps the formation together.

Standing on the fortress wall, the valley is surveyed and riders are sent to the flanks. Victory depends on holding the road below Mtskheta until the armored reserve can be unleashed. Once the enemy line gives way, the cavalry wings will sweep its sides. Each noble house keeps a record of which men were lost, and the record will matter when the land is divided.
